reason: A short `\u` escape on line 2 of a long string reports line 2, column 4 (#521; `_unescape`, `_Lexer.locate`). It raises from the hex-digit branch of `_unescape`, not the unknown-escape statement of test_provn_lexer.py::test_string_escape_error_position, so it stays out of that merge.

Short hex, lowercase hex, non-scalar values, unknown IRI escapes and IRI-forbidden characters each raise at the escape (#521, #729, #509; `_unescape`, `_IRI_FORBIDDEN`). Each row has its own message format or branch.

A raw CR inside a short string or a quoted name makes it unterminated, because `_SHORT_STRING` and `_QNAME_LITERAL`, matched in `_Lexer.string_token` and `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, exclude CR. Its rows are the unescaped counterpart of the backslash-CR rows of test_provn_lexer.py::test_malformed_input_reports_position.
`\u` and `\U` escapes decode in strings and IRIs, and `\\u` stays literal (#521, #729; `_unescape`, `_ESCAPE`).

`//` and `/* */` comments are dropped between tokens by `tokenize` (the `_SKIP` pattern in `_Lexer.tokens`). Without it a comment would reach the parser as a token. Its lone-CR sibling is test_provn_lexer.py::test_line_comment_ends_at_cr_not_just_lf.

A backslash escape in a local part is accepted for exactly the PN_CHARS_ESC characters and rejected, at column 6, for every other printable ASCII character and two Latin-1 ones (#729). Each row is a different character against one character class (`_ESC`, `_PN_LOCAL`, `_QNAME`, `_qname_value`), so an edit to the class changes one row.
A 5000-digit integer raises `ProvNSyntaxError` naming the digit limit, not `ValueError` (`_Lexer._int_value`). A raw `int()` would crash the reader on hostile input.
`"a"@` raises "invalid language tag" from `_Lexer.langtag_token` (`_LANGTAG`). It guards the failure branch of the tag reader.
An IRI may hold U+00A0 but not `\x01` (`_IRI` and `_IRI_EXCLUDED`, matched in `_Lexer.iri_token`). It guards both the accept and the reject side of the IRI character class.

`_Lexer.next_token` reads `@en` as a language tag only when the previous token is a string, and as part of a name elsewhere (`_Lexer.langtag_token`). It is the lexer's one context-sensitive rule, and a change that dropped the check would turn `ex:a@b` into a name and a tag.

Token line and column after LF, CRLF and CR breaks, inside long strings and inside block comments (`_Lexer.advance_lines`, `_Lexer._line_after`, `_Lexer.emit`, `_LINEBREAK`). Each row has its own break kind or token type, so a fault in one counting path fails one row.

A `//` comment ends at a lone CR, as the Recommendation's comment note says (`_SKIP`, matched in `_Lexer.tokens`). A lone CR is its own input shape beside test_provn_lexer.py::test_comments_are_skipped.

`_QNAME` and `_qname_value` turn one spelling of a name into a (prefix, local) pair: a percent escape (`_PERCENT`), an escaped dot, colon or hyphen at the end of a local part (`_LOCAL_LAST`), an inner dot in a local part (`_LOCAL_CONT`) or in a prefix (`_PN_PREFIX`), and a bare name with the empty prefix. Folds in test_provn_lexer.py::test_percent_encoding_is_kept_verbatim, test_escaped_dot_is_kept, test_inner_dot_is_part_of_the_name, test_escaped_colon_at_end_of_local_part, test_escaped_hyphen_in_local_part (section 3.8 example), test_prefix_with_inner_dot_is_still_accepted and test_bare_local_name_has_empty_prefix. All seven asserted `values(text) == [(prefix, local)]`, so only the input and the expected pair moved into rows and nothing was lost. The prefix row still guards `_PN_PREFIX` against over-rejection beside test_provn_lexer.py::test_prefix_cannot_end_in_a_dot.

A million trailing dots fail within a time bound, so `_LOCAL_LAST` and `_PN_LOCAL`, matched through `_QNAME` in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`, stay linear. A quadratic back-off would pass every test that has no time bound.

Each malformed input raises `ProvNSyntaxError` with the right line, column and the text "line N, column M" (#509; `_Lexer.error`, `_Lexer.next_token`, `_Lexer.string_token`, `_Lexer.iri_token`, `_Lexer.name_token`, `_unescape`). The 24 `NON_WS_SPACES` rows meet different character classes (`_PN_CHARS`, `_PN_CHARS_U`), so a class edit can change one row.
`-` alone is a marker, `-5` is an integer and `- 5` is a marker then an integer, which depends on `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` running before the marker branch of `_Lexer.next_token`.
Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits are name characters, not integers, because PROV-N DIGIT is `[0-9]` (`_INT`, `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`). The two rows are two code-point blocks.
The error for U+00A0 reads "U+00A0 is not PROV-N whitespace" (#509; `_Lexer.next_token`). test_provn.py::test_reader_rejects reaches the same message through the parser, a different entry point.

`NON_WS_SPACES` plus U+1680 equals every `str.isspace` code point outside space, tab, CR and LF (#509). It runs no `src/prov` code and keeps the oracle list behind test_provn_lexer.py::test_malformed_input_reports_position complete.
U+1680 starts a name and is not a separator (#509; `_Lexer.next_token`, which comments on U+1680).

The derived PN_CHARS classes equal the Recommendation's literal ranges over every non-surrogate code point (#668; `_PN_CHARS_U`, `_PN_CHARS` in `provn_lexer`, and `_PN_CHARS_BASE`, `_PN_CHARS_ESC` in `identifier`). The contract is real. Only the access to the private names is not.

A prefix that ends in a dot is rejected at or after the dot (PROV-N PN_PREFIX; #668; `_PN_PREFIX` in `_QNAME`, matched in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`). It pairs with the inner-dot prefix row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings.

`entity(bbc:)` reads `bbc:` as a name with an empty local part, the Recommendation's own example, through the optional local part of `_QNAME` in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`. It asserts the first four tokens of a statement, so it is not a row of test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings.

`ProvNSyntaxError` is a public exception and survives pickle and deepcopy with its line, column and message intact (`ProvNSyntaxError.__reduce__`). A `__reduce__` that dropped an argument would break copying across processes.

A quoted name that `_QNAME_FULL` rejects raises from `_split_qname` at the end of the partial `_QNAME` match: column 5 for a space after a bare name, column 8 for a space inside a prefixed name, and column 8 for a trailing dot. Folds in test_provn_lexer.py::test_invalid_qname_literal_raises, test_qname_literal_error_position_is_the_first_invalid_character and test_qname_literal_trailing_dot_raises. Every input and assertion stays, so nothing was lost. The row `space-after-bare-name` is named for its input, because a bare `not` alone is a valid name.
A quoted qualified name decodes `\'` into its local part through `_Lexer.qname_literal_token`, `_split_qname` and `_qname_value`.

A bare trailing dot on a local part raises at the dot's column, because a PN_LOCAL cannot end in a dot (`_LOCAL_LAST`, `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`, `_Lexer.next_token`). The position check is exact where test_provn_lexer.py::test_prefix_cannot_end_in_a_dot checks `>=`, and this input is a local part, not a prefix.

An unknown `\q` escape raises from the one statement in `_unescape` that rejects it, and `_Lexer.locate` puts the error at the escape: column 2 of `"\q"`, column 6 inside a short string, and line 2 column 4 in a long string. Folds in test_provn_lexer.py::test_unknown_string_escape_raises, test_string_escape_error_position_is_inside_the_literal and test_string_escape_error_position_spans_lines_in_a_long_string. Every input and assertion stays, and `match=None` asserts what leaving out `match` did, so nothing was lost. The issue citation of the classifier (#521, the code point escapes) does not match these inputs.

Short and long strings decode `\\`, `\"` and `\t` in `_unescape` through `_STRING_ESCAPES`, and a long string (`_LONG_STRING`) keeps inner quotes. Without it a string would reach the parser with its escapes undecoded.
`Token` is public through `__all__`, so its hash and equality by field and its lack of a `__dict__` are part of the contract. A `Token` that lost `unsafe_hash` or `slots` would change both.

`tokenize` gives each token class (name, string, integer, datetime, IRI and the punctuation) its `TokenKind`, through the dispatch order of `_Lexer.next_token` and `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token`. A reordered branch would label one input kind wrongly and go unnoticed here. The row ids follow the PROV-N Recommendation's lexical productions.
`%%` between tokens is the typed-literal marker, while `%41` inside a name stays in the name (`_Lexer.next_token` against `_PERCENT`). A lexer that read every `%` as a marker would split names.

Non-ASCII names tokenise through `_PN_CHARS_U` in `_Lexer.literal_or_name_token` and a non-ASCII string through `_SHORT_STRING` in `_Lexer.string_token`. The judge ruled that it stays unfolded, because the string assertion pins a STRING token, and a row under test_provn_lexer.py::test_local_part_and_prefix_spellings would label it a name spelling. The maintainer accepted the ruling.
An open `/*` raises "unterminated comment" at the opener, from the `startswith("/*")` check in `_Lexer.tokens`.
Tab, CRLF, NBSP and U+3000 inside comments, strings and IRIs, and between tokens, raise nothing (#509; `_SKIP`, `_Lexer.next_token`). It guards against over-rejection beside the whitespace rule.
